answer: A practical defence is stake-backed identity with slow reputation: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before transacting, and trust only grows through verified, useful work over time. Creating fake identities then requires capital for every copy, while misconduct forfeits the deposit and resets reputation. Like an island reached only by paying for each crossing, or an opal checked before trade, quantity becomes expensive and quality scarce. A violet audit trail can link suspicious clusters, so an attacker must spend money and time per identity rather than cloning them free.
